s1.title: Under cloud
s1.caption: July. Optical satellites see only cloud.

s2.fig: Fig. 2 — Sentinel-1 VH backscatter, one paddy pixel, {year}
s2.title: Radar sees through
s2.caption: Radar sees through cloud. Flooding a paddy makes VH backscatter drop; the growing crop brings it back.

s3.fig: Fig. 3 — Median transplant date by upazila, 2017–2025
s3.title: Where they planted
s3.caption: Each upazila’s median transplant date, detected by radar pixel by pixel.

s4.title: The rain moved
s4.caption: Usable monsoon rain is arriving later. Trend tested with Mann-Kendall; slope by Sen, with its 95% interval.

s5.fig: Fig. 5 — Adaptation gap: transplant date − rain onset
s5.title: The adaptation gap
s5.caption: The adaptation gap: days from usable-rain onset to transplanting. Is planting keeping pace with the rain?

s6.title: Field replay
s6.caption: Every detection can be inspected, including pixels where the rule should refuse to answer.

s7.title: The advice
s7.caption: Findings become advice a farmer can act on: in Bangla, by SMS, with an honest confidence label.

s8.title: Evidence
s8.caption: Every number traces back to its data and its method.

s3.revisitNote12: Only Sentinel-1A flying: fewer acquisitions, fewer confident detections.

s4.rule: Onset rule: first day from 1 June with ≥ 20 mm over 3 days and no dry spell > 7 days in the next 30.

s5.note: 9 seasons — per-year gap shown, no trend claimed.
